nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-mcgr.name: Christine McGrath
nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-mcgr.bio: Verona Town Council member since 2019 with 25 years of professional communications experience.

positions.stance: "Ensuring fiscal oversight that protects taxpayers during challenging economic cycles."
Strengthening county-local collaboration "to keep our neighborhoods safe and our roads and parks thriving."
Bringing proactive communication to the County Board "to ensure you always know how your tax dollars are being spent."

nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-yasi.name: Abdur R. Yasin
nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-yasi.bio: Fire captain, college lecturer, and Democratic chair.

positions.stance: Committed to responsible budgeting, cutting waste, and efficient government so residents "can keep more of what they earn."
Will work to improve roads, invest in transportation, and modernize infrastructure.
Will "stand with labor," support fair wages, and advocate for policies that protect workers and create good-paying jobs.
Will work with law enforcement and community leaders to reduce crime, strengthen trust, and ensure every neighborhood feels safe.

nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-enge.name: Deborah Engel
nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-enge.bio: Former Maplewood Deputy Mayor and Township Committee member and small business founder.

positions.stance: Supports shared and regional services, responsible county budgeting, and housing to reduce financial pressure on families and municipalities.
Supports complete streets, pedestrian and bicycle safety, and expanded transit options.
Supports "standing up for immigrant families, opposing harmful ICE activity and detention," and confronting hate and discrimination.
Supports regional solutions to flooding and stormwater, protecting tree canopy and open space, and preparing infrastructure for a changing climate.
Supports clear communication and "greater transparency around county spending and decisions."

wa-snohomish-2026-prosecutor-cummings-ja.name: Jason Cummings
wa-snohomish-2026-prosecutor-cummings-ja.bio: Snohomish County Prosecuting Attorney (first term) after nearly 25 years as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney, including 14 years as Chief Civil Deputy.

md-anne-arundel-2026-exec-pickard-alliso.name: Allison M. Pickard
md-anne-arundel-2026-exec-pickard-alliso.bio: Anne Arundel County Council member since 2018; former AmeriCorps team leader.

positions.stance: Will fight for a county where working families can afford to live, including expanding affordable housing and lowering the tax burden on working families.
Pledges to fully implement the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, increase teacher pay, and add teaching positions to reduce class sizes.
Supports expanding workforce development and job training, improving transportation connectivity, and building partnerships with schools, unions, and employers.
Supports small business growth, attracting good-paying jobs, revitalizing commercial corridors, and fixing "the broken permitting process."
Will invest in climate resilience and flood prevention, protect green spaces and waterways, and expand clean energy initiatives.

md-anne-arundel-2026-exec-crawford-dave.name: Dave Crawford
md-anne-arundel-2026-exec-crawford-dave.bio: Chief of the Earleigh Heights Volunteer Fire Company with a 40-year career in business.

positions.stance: Will prioritize increasing police and fire personnel for faster response times and make better use of reserve officers.
Will work to eliminate wasteful spending, ensure tax dollars are used efficiently, and push for business investment and better-paying jobs.
Will cut wasteful spending and expand housing options for individuals, working families, and seniors through responsible development.
Will start a Senior Promise Program, strengthen veterans' support, enhance county ride services, and invest in smarter road maintenance.
Will seek to expand trained school resource officers so every school has "a visible and trusted layer of protection."

md-anne-arundel-2026-sa-leitess-anne.name: Anne Colt Leitess
md-anne-arundel-2026-sa-leitess-anne.bio: Career prosecutor for over 30 years; Anne Arundel County State's Attorney, first appointed in 2013 and elected in 2018 and 2022.

positions.stance: Says she is willing to "speak out against the abuses of ICE" during "troubling times of federal overreach."
Says the office "seeks treatment and rehabilitation for non-violent and youthful offenders."
"When it comes to public safety and violent crime-we prosecute those who endanger our community."

md-anne-arundel-2026-register-jackson-ja.name: Jasmine M. Jackson
md-anne-arundel-2026-register-jackson-ja.bio: Anne Arundel County Register of Wills since her June 2024 appointment; has worked in the Register of Wills office since 2008.

md-anne-arundel-2026-sheriff-sesker-ever.name: Everett Sesker
md-anne-arundel-2026-sheriff-sesker-ever.bio: Anne Arundel County Sheriff; retired as a Major after 22 years with the Prince George's County Police Department and former Executive Director of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.

positions.stance: Moving the Sheriff's Office to "a more innovative, 21st century approach to leadership."
"Reducing time and cost through the proper allocation of resources."
"Meeting community expectations through research based training and evaluation."
"Visibility through continuous community engagement and communication."

md-anne-arundel-2026-sheriff-fredericks-.name: Jim Fredericks
md-anne-arundel-2026-sheriff-fredericks-.bio: Former Anne Arundel County Sheriff (elected 2018) after 26 years with the Anne Arundel County Police Department.

positions.stance: "Add new partnerships to enhance courthouse security."
"Expand the number of deputies available for courtroom safety."
"Restore and renew relationships with our law enforcement partners."
"Reinstate lost positions of accountability."
"Prioritize reducing the backlog of outstanding warrants."

md-baltimore-county-2026-exec-jones-juli.name: Julian Jones
md-baltimore-county-2026-exec-jones-juli.bio: Baltimore County Council member since 2014 and three-time Council Chairman; former Anne Arundel County Fire Department division chief.

positions.stance: "Keeping our neighborhoods safe through smart policing and community partnerships."
"Investing in our children's future with modern schools and workforce training."
"Creating opportunities for job growth and supporting local businesses."
"Lowering bills, restoring local control, and protecting families from rising energy costs."
